entity_title: CSEP holder's right to bring immediate family (spouse + minor children)
fact_text: A Critical Skills Employment Permit (CSEP) holder can apply for immediate family reunification from the Immigration Service Delivery (ISD) — there is no waiting period before the CSEP holder's family can apply to join them in Ireland.
evidence_quote: Permit holders can apply for immediate family reunification from the Immigration Service Delivery (ISD) of the Department of Justice and Equality

entity_title: Financial thresholds and policy conditions for family sponsorship
fact_text: A Critical Skills Employment Permit (CSEP) holder is a Category B sponsor for family reunification purposes. For Category B sponsors, no specific gross income threshold over a cumulative three-year period applies (unlike Category A Irish citizens who need €75,000 over three years), because the immigration status granted assumes certain levels of income either immediately or in the future, or because the sponsor falls into a category whose migration to Ireland is promoted as part of Government policy.
evidence_quote: For Category B sponsors (e.g. Critical Skills Employment Permit holder or researcher), the immigration status granted assumes certain levels of income either immediately or in the future or on the basis that the sponsor falls into a category whose migration to Ireland is promoted as part of Government policy.

entity_title: Spouse's Stamp 1G and right to work without an employment permit
fact_text: Since 6 March 2019, the spouse or de-facto partner of a CSEP holder does NOT need an employment permit to work in Ireland. ISD grants them a Stamp 1 immigration permission which provides direct access to the labour market.
evidence_quote: Since 6 March 2019, the requirement for spouses and de-facto partners of Critical Employment Permit (CSEP) Holders and Researchers under a Hosting Agreement as provided for under the EU Third Country Researchers Directive (Council Directive 2005/71/EC) to obtain an employment permit has been removed by the Department of Enterprise, Trade and Employment.

entity_title: Spouse's Stamp 1G and right to work without an employment permit
fact_text: The spouse or de-facto partner of a CSEP holder is granted Stamp 1 immigration permission by ISD, which gives direct access to the Irish labour market without needing an employment permit.
evidence_quote: The Immigration Service Delivery (ISD) will grant eligible spouses and de-facto partners of CSEP holders and Researchers under a Hosting Agreement permission to reside in this State on Stamp 1 Conditions which provides direct access to the labour market without the need to obtain an employment permit.

entity_title: Dependant children's immigration permission (under-16 vs 16–18 registration)
fact_text: Dependent children of a CSEP holder are issued a Stamp 3 immigration permission by ISD. Stamp 3 does not of itself entitle a foreign national to work; only those Stamp 3 holders accompanying the CSEP holder as a dependant can apply for a Dependant Employment Permit to work.
evidence_quote: A dependant of a Critical Skills Employment Permit Holder is issued with a Stamp 3 immigration permission by the Immigration Service Delivery (ISD). A Stamp 3 permission does not, of itself, entitle a foreign national to work.

entity_title: Dependant children's immigration permission (under-16 vs 16–18 registration)
fact_text: Dependants of a CSEP holder who wish to work in Ireland can apply for a Dependant Employment Permit. This permit is issued free of charge, does not require a Labour Market Needs Test, covers all jobs except domestic operative, and remuneration must be at or above the National Minimum Wage.
evidence_quote: This Dependant Employment Permit has a number of benefits including: The application is free of charge. All jobs are eligible for a Dependant Employment Permit, except that of domestic operative. Remuneration must be at, or above, the National Minimum Wage. The prospective employer is not required to undertake a Labour Market Needs Test, that is, advertise the position.

entity_title: Spouse's Stamp 1G and right to work without an employment permit
fact_text: A person holding Stamp 1G in Ireland does not need an employment permit to work. This stamp is relevant to spouses/partners of CSEP holders who have converted from their initial Stamp 1 after the CSEP holder's permit expires and they obtain permission to reside and work without an employment permit.
evidence_quote:
You don't need an employment permit to work in Ireland while you have the following residence stamps:
Stamp 1G
Stamp 4, 4S, 4D or 4EUFAM
Stamp 5

entity_title: Spouse's Stamp 1G and right to work without an employment permit
fact_text: A CSEP holder may apply to Irish immigration for permission to reside and work without the requirement for an employment permit upon completion of the Critical Skills Employment Permit's duration.
evidence_quote: Permit holders may apply to the Irish Naturalisation and Immigration Service for permission to reside and work without the requirement for an employment permit upon completion of the Critical Skills Employment Permit's duration.

entity_title: Join Family ‘D’ long-stay visa (process, documents, fees)
fact_text: Venezuelans are visa-required nationals. A family member who wishes to stay in Ireland for more than 3 months must apply for a long stay 'D' visa before travelling.
evidence_quote: If you want to stay in Ireland for longer than 3 months, you apply for a 'D' visa.

entity_title: Join Family ‘D’ long-stay visa (process, documents, fees)
fact_text: A non-EEA family member wishing to join a non-EEA national (such as a CSEP holder) who is lawfully resident in Ireland must apply for a long stay (join family) visa.
evidence_quote: If you wish to come to Ireland to reside for more than 3 months with a family member who is a non-EEA or non-Swiss national who is lawfully resident in Ireland you can apply for a long stay (join family) visa.

entity_title: IRP registration of family members after arrival
fact_text: Any non-EU/EEA and non-Swiss national who comes to Ireland to work, study, live or join family for more than 90 days must register with Immigration Service Delivery to get an Irish Residence Permit (IRP card).
evidence_quote: If you are from a country outside the European Union, UK or Switzerland, and come to Ireland to work, study, live or join family for more than 90 days, you must register with Immigration Service Delivery.

entity_title: IRP registration of family members after arrival
fact_text: Registration with ISD records that a person has been given a permission to stay in Ireland and what they can legally do while there. Family members must register after arriving on a long stay D visa.
evidence_quote: Registration is how we record that you have been given a permission to stay in Ireland and what you can legally do while you are here.

entity_title: IRP registration of family members after arrival
fact_text: A family member who arrives in Ireland on a long stay 'D' visa and wishes to stay longer than 3 months must visit the registration office in Dublin or at a local Garda station outside of Dublin, before their landing stamp expires, to extend their immigration permission and register.
evidence_quote: If you arrive with a long stay 'D' visa and wish to stay longer than 3 months, you must visit the registration office in Dublin or at a local Garda station outside of Dublin, before your landing stamp expires to extend your immigration permission and register your details.

entity_title: Dependant children's immigration permission (under-16 vs 16–18 registration)
fact_text: Children under 16 do not need to register with ISD (and thus do not need an IRP card) unless they are non-EEA citizens joining under EU Treaty Rights. However, children under 16 may still need to apply for a visa to enter Ireland.
evidence_quote:
Children under 16 do not need to register with ISD unless they are non-EEA citizens joining you under EU Treaty Rights.
Note: Children under 16 may need to apply for a visa to enter the country.

entity_title: Dependant children's immigration permission (under-16 vs 16–18 registration)
fact_text: Children aged between 16 and 18 (or under 23 and in full-time education) who are non-EEA nationals must register with ISD if they are not Irish, British, Swiss or EEA citizens.
evidence_quote: If you have children aged between 16 and 18, or under 23 and in fulltime education, they must register with ISD if they are not Irish, British, Swiss or EEA citizens.

entity_title: Join Family ‘D’ long-stay visa (process, documents, fees)
fact_text: The Dependant Employment Permit available to dependants of CSEP holders who wish to work in Ireland is issued free of charge.
evidence_quote: once their dependants/partners/spouses are resident in the State they are eligible to seek any employment and apply to the Department of Enterprise, Trade and Employment for a Dependant/Partner/Spouse Employment Permit which is currently issued free of charge.

entity_title: Financial thresholds and policy conditions for family sponsorship
fact_text: Category B sponsors for family reunification (who benefit from more favourable financial threshold treatment) include: Critical Skills Employment Permit (CSEP) holders, Intra-company transferees, Full-time non-locum doctors in employment, Researchers on Hosting Agreements, Investors on the Immigrant Investor Programme (IIP), Entrepreneurs on the Start-up Entrepreneur Programme (STEP), ISD-approved scholarship programme students, PhD student permission holders, and Ministers of Religion.
evidence_quote: Category B: Critical Skills Employment Permit (CSEP) holders, Intra-company transferees, Full-time non-locum doctors in employment, Researchers on Hosting Agreements, Investors on the Immigrant Investor Programme (IIP), Entrepreneurs on the Start-up Entrepreneur Programme (STEP), ISD-approved scholarship programme students (e.g. KASP), PhD student permission holders (subject to additional conditions), Ministers of Religion under the relevant scheme (subject to additional conditions).

entity_title: CSEP holder's right to bring immediate family (spouse + minor children)
fact_text: A dependant of a CSEP holder must have resided in Ireland on a continuous basis since landing, must not be in full-time education, and must reside with the primary permit holder. Applications for Employment Permits for a dependant residing outside Ireland will not be accepted.

entity_title: Financial thresholds and policy conditions for family sponsorship
fact_text: Only the income of one sponsor is considered for family reunification financial thresholds — the CSEP holder cannot combine their salary with that of a spouse, partner or any other family member to reach thresholds.
evidence_quote: only the income of one sponsor will be considered, so you cannot combine your salary with that of your spouse, partner or any other family member to reach these thresholds.

entity_title: Financial thresholds and policy conditions for family sponsorship
fact_text: Applications submitted on or after 12 June 2026 are subject to the June 2026 Non-EEA Family Reunification Policy Document. The policy was previously revised on 26 November 2025.
evidence_quote: If you submit your application on or after 12 June 2026, your application is subject to the June 2026 Non-EEA Family Reunification Policy Document.
